In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat at-Tur

It is a Meccan surah. It is established, by the narration of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, that he said: "I heard the Prophet recite Surat at-Tur in the Maghrib prayer."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By the Mount (at-Tur)﴾. Mujahid said: it is, in Syriac, the name for a mountain. The more correct view is that it is the name of the mountain in Arabic. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: every mountain that grows vegetation is a tur, and whatever does not grow vegetation is not a tur. Ka'b al-Ahbar and others said: it is the Tur upon which Allah spoke to Musa. This view has also been reported from Qatadah and 'Ikrimah. And from Nawf al-Bikali: Allah the Exalted revealed to the mountains, "Indeed I will send down [a revelation] upon one mountain among you," so the mountains lifted up their heads in pride, while at-Tur humbled itself and said: "I am content with what Allah has apportioned to me." And the matter was as he said.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿And a written Book﴾ — there are several opinions on it. It is said that it is the Qur'an, and this is related from al-Hasan al-Basri. The second: it is the Torah, which Allah the Exalted wrote on the tablets. The third: it is the Book in which Allah recorded the deeds of the children of Adam, and it will be brought out on the Day of Resurrection and become scrolls; so one will take his (record) in his right hand, and one will take his in his left, and one will take his behind his back. This is a well-known opinion, mentioned by al-Farra' and others.

It is also said that what is meant by it is the scrolls from which the angels read in the heaven, the Qur'an, according to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿In scrolls held in honour, exalted, purified, in the hands of scribes﴾. And it is said that it is the Preserved Tablet, in which has been written whatever is to happen until the Day of Resurrection.

"And His saying: ﴿in a scroll unrolled﴾. Al-raqq is the parchment on which a thing is written.

And His saying: ﴿unrolled﴾, i.e., spread out. This supports the view we mentioned, that the Book is the records of deeds in the Hereafter, because Allah, exalted is He, said in another place: ﴿And when the pages are spread open﴾, and what is meant by it is the records of deeds in the Hereafter."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 4:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And the House that is frequented﴾. Some of them said: it is the Ka'bah, and its being frequented is through the Hajj and the circumambulation (tawaf). The well-known view is that it is a House in the heavens. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of the exegetes (mufassirun), and it is also narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

They differed regarding its location. Anas ibn Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah narrated from the Prophet, in the account of the Mi'raj (Night Ascent), that he said: "The House that is frequented was raised up for me in the seventh heaven."

And from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that it is in the sixth heaven. And from al-Rabi' ibn Anas and others, that it is in the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya), directly opposite the Ka'bah, so that if it were to fall, it would fall upon it.

In the narrative: the House that is frequented was sent down by Allah the Most High from the heaven to Adam, and He placed it in the location of the Ka'bah. When the time of Noah came, Allah the Most High raised it to the lowest heaven, and it is the place of pilgrimage (hajj) for the angels, and its sanctity is like the sanctity of the Ka'bah on earth.

'Ali and others said: its name is al-Darah'. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they never return to it again. This wording has been traced back to the Messenger.

And some of them said that it is in the fourth heaven. In some of the musnad collections: "Allah the Most High created a river beneath the Throne called the River of Life. Jibril, peace be upon him, enters it every day when the sun rises, then comes out and shakes himself, and seventy thousand drops fall from him; Allah the Most High creates from each drop an angel, and they populate the House that is frequented." This is a strange report (khabar gharib).
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the raised canopy﴾. On this there are two opinions. One: that it is the sky. The other: that it is the Throne.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿And the sea that is filled (al-masjur)﴾. The most well-known of the opinions regarding it is that it is the full one. And it is related from Rabi' ibn Anas, concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾, that he said: Indeed Allah, exalted is He, made that water into two halves when He created the heavens and the earth. He made one half of it beneath the seventh earth and one half of it beneath the Throne. So when it is between the two blasts, Allah will send down from it a rain upon the earth, and by it the bodies will grow in the graves.

The second opinion regarding the verse: that the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur) is the one that has been made to overflow (al-mafjur), as Allah, exalted is He, said in another place: ﴿And when the seas are made to overflow﴾. Their being made to overflow is their being spread out and released over the earth. And it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The sea that is filled is the one that is released, and that is for the meaning we have explained.

The third opinion: that the sea that is filled is the one that has been kindled with fire, from their saying: "I heated the oven" (sajartu al-tannur). And it is related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "Where is Hell?" He said: "It is the sea." So he said: "I see you are only truthful," and he recited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

The fourth opinion: that the sea that is filled is the sea whose water has dried up and gone, as though the seas of the earth will be emptied of water on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them expressed this sea that is filled as "the empty one."

Almost there: the Lord's words, "Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur" (﴿إِن عَذَاب رَبك لوَاقِع﴾). The oath falls upon this statement, and up to this point it was an oath in the sense we mentioned in the preceding surah.

His words "﴿واقع﴾" mean: "kā'in" (existent, bound to take place).

The phrase ﴿What he has no one to repel it﴾ means: there is no one among the disbelievers who can repel it.

It is related from Jubayr ibn Mut'im that he came to Madinah intending to ransom some of the captives of Badr. He heard the Prophet (ﷺ) reciting Surah al-Tur in the prayer, and when he heard His words, ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to occur; there is none to repel it﴾, he was overcome, trembling and fearful, and that was the cause of his Islam.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 52, verse 9:

His words: ﴿On the Day when the sky will sway violently to and fro﴾. That is: it will revolve (tadur). It is also said: it will come and go, and what is meant is its movement. It is also said: it will be overturned with its inhabitants (tukfa'u bi-ahliha).

And His saying ﴿And the mountains will move, moving﴾ means: they will come and go over the surface of the earth. It is also said: their movement will be like the movement of clouds between the sky and the earth, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will pass by like the passing of clouds﴾.

Then woe on that day to the deniers, who are at play in their idle discourse. It is said: they plunge into the matter of the Prophet with denial, and they make sport of what is serious (al-jadd). It is related from some of them that he was seen in a dream, and it was said to him: "What is the matter?" He said: "The matter is serious, so beware of mixing it with jest." It was also said: God, exalted is He, made everything they are engaged in a game.

Then woe on that day to the deniers, who are at play in their idle discourse. It is said: they plunge into the matter of the Prophet with denial, and they make sport of what is serious (al-jadd). It is related from some of them that he was seen in a dream, and it was said to him: "What is the matter?" He said: "The matter is serious, so beware of mixing it with jest." It was also said: God, exalted is He, made everything they are engaged in a game.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day they will be thrust into the fire of Hell, a thrusting﴾. That is: they will be pushed into the Fire of Hell.

And His saying: ﴿دَعَا﴾ means: pushing. Linguistically, الدع (al-da') is pushing with force and violence.
And His saying: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny﴾ — this is said to them by way of rebuke and reproach.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 15:

Regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿Is this magic? Or is it you who do not see?﴾ In the tafsir (commentary): when they used to see the signs in this world and the proofs of the Messenger's prophethood, they would say, "They are magic, and we do not perceive what he says," meaning, "we do not know." So when the Day of Resurrection comes and they witness the punishment, it will be said to them: "Is this magic, as you claimed in the world, because of the signs you saw? Or is it that you do not see?" That is, "Are you not seeing, just as you did not see in the world according to your claim?"

The second opinion regarding His words ﴿Or is it that you do not see?﴾ is that its meaning is "rather, you used to not see," meaning "you used not to know." This is a well-known view.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 16:

And His saying: ﴿Burn therein [isluhā]﴾, meaning: enter it. It is also said: "Taste its heat" (qasu harraha).

And His saying: ﴿So be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you﴾ is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is all the same for us whether we lament or we are patient﴾. The meaning is: whether you are patient or whether you rage, it is all the same for you, for the punishment is befalling you and will not be lightened for you. It is related in some reports that the people of the Fire will lament for a long period, calling out upon themselves with "woe" and "destruction," then they will say: "Come, let us be patient," and they will be patient for a long period as well, but neither of the two will benefit them. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is all the same for you﴾, that is: both states are equal, and the punishment is continuous upon you in both of them.

And His saying: ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾ means: this is your own deed, produced by yourselves.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and bliss.﴾ That is: gardens and blessing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 18:

And His saying: ﴿fakihin﴾ (enjoying). Ibn 'Arafa, who is Nifṭawayh the grammarian, said: fakihin means "living in luxury" (na'imin). It is also said: fakihin means "possessing fruit" (dhawi fakiha). It is said: "Fulan la-ibn," meaning "he possesses milk" (dhu laban), and "tamir," meaning "he possesses dates" (dhu tamr). It has also been read as ﴿fakihin﴾ (fakihin), meaning "delighted, pleased with their state."

And His saying: ﴿bima atahum rabbuhum﴾ (with what their Lord has given them), meaning: what their Lord has bestowed upon them.

And His saying: ﴿wa waqahum rabbuhum 'adhaba l-jahim﴾ (and their Lord has protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire), meaning: the punishment of the Fire. Al-Jahim: the great mass of the Fire.

The Exalted One's saying: ﴿Eat and drink with ease﴾, meaning: "you enjoy it" (تهنئون) "هَنِيئًا" (with ease, without hardship).

And His saying: ﴿because of what you used to do﴾, meaning: what you used to do of "الطَّاعَات" (acts of obedience).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 20:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Reclining on couches﴾ (sururin), is the plural of sarir (couch).

And His saying: ﴿arranged in rows﴾ means that some of them are joined to others. It is also said: masta, (variant reading) "arranged in rows" (musṭaffa).

In the tafsir it is related that the height of the couch is such-and-such miles, and when the believer wishes to mount it, it lowers itself until the believer can reach it, then it returns to what it was.

And His saying: ﴿and We will pair them with∗ companions﴾ means: We will join them with (qaranahum). This was said by al-Farra', al-Zajjaj and others among the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani). They said: What is meant is not the marriage (tazwij) known in this world, for the contract of marriage is among the contracts of this world and not among the contracts of the Hereafter.

And His saying: ﴿with wide-eyed houris (bi-hurin 'in)﴾. Al-hawr means whiteness, and from it comes al-hawari (a white-clothed helper), and from it al-hawariyyun (the disciples) of 'Isa, who were the launderers who whiten clothes. The Arabs call the women of the cities hawariyat because of their fairness.

Some of them said:

(So she said to the fair ones who weep for other than us... and none weeps for us except the barking dogs.)

And His saying: ﴿'in﴾ means: beautiful of eye (hisan al-'ayn). It is said: each one of them is called hawra' because of the intensity of her whiteness and the blackness of her (pupils).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 21:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We shall join their descendants with them﴾. It is also read: "wa-ittaba'athum dhurriyyatuhum" (and their descendants followed them). In a report, stopped at Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf) and traced back to the Messenger of Allah (marfu'): "Allah the Exalted raises the descendants of the believer to his rank, even if their deeds do not reach it, so that their eyes may be delighted by them." Some scholars said that this applies to fathers with their children and to children with their fathers together, as if Allah brings the father up to the rank of the child if the child is higher in rank, and brings the child up to the rank of the father if the father is higher in rank. It is also reported in some books that this applies also to a brother with his brother in faith: the brother says, "O Lord, raise him to my rank," and He says, "He did not do deeds like yours," and He says, "I did deeds for myself and for him."

In some reports from the Prophet: "The children of the believers will be with their fathers in Paradise, and the children of the disbelievers with their fathers in Hell." (﴿With faith, We join their descendants to them﴾.) In some reports: "The children of the polytheists will be servants of the people of Paradise." It is established by the narration of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that a boy from the Ansar died, and 'A'ishah said, "Blessed is he, a sparrow of the sparrows of Paradise." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said, "O 'A'ishah, or other than that? Allah the Exalted created the Fire and created for it its people, and He created them for it while they were in their fathers' loins; and He created Paradise and created for it its people, and He created them for it while they were in their fathers' loins."

The Shaykh, the Imam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, informed us of this in Makkah; Abu al-Hasan ibn Faras informed us; Abu Muhammad al-Muqri' informed us; my grandfather informed us, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'A'ishah bint Talhah, from 'A'ishah, mother of the believers, from the Prophet... And the report is in Sahih Muslim.

The scholars have said: the more correct view concerning the offspring of the believers is that they are in Paradise. It is possible that the Prophet said that only according to what he knew at first; then Allah the Exalted informed him that the offspring of the Muslims are in Paradise, by this verse and others. As for the offspring of the disbelievers, the more correct view is to suspend judgment about them, in line with what is reported from the Prophet that he was asked about the children of the polytheists and said: "Allah knows best what they would have done."

His words ﴿with faith﴾ mean: with their faith, either by their own faith, or by the establishment of faith for them through the faith of the fathers.

﴿We shall join their descendants with them﴾ means: in rank, as we have said.

His words ﴿And We shall not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ mean: We shall not reduce anything of their deeds. Ibn Kathir read "wa-ma alatnahum" with a kasra on the lam, and the first (alatnahum, with fatha) is the better. Ibn Mas'ud read "wa-ma latnahum," and both have the same meaning.

The poet said:

(Convey to the Banu Thaqif from me a message, delivered with full effort, neither diminished nor false.)

His words ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾ are about the polytheists, and their meaning is that the disbelievers are confined in the Fire by their deeds. As for the believer, he is not confined or held in pledge; but if he is held in pledge by his deed, he must enter the Fire. In the well-known report, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "No one among you will be saved by his deed." It was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We will provide them with fruit⁠—﴾. This is a return to the description of the people of Paradise.

And His saying: ﴿and meat of fowl, from whatever they desire﴾ is clear in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 23:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿They will pass around among themselves a cup﴾. That is, they will hand it to one another (ta'ātī, passing the cup), and the meaning is that some of them give to others as drinking is done in this world.

Imru' al-Qays said:

(When we engaged in talk and he became generous, I bent down to a branch with clustered fruit, drooping.)

﴿Therein there will be no idle talk nor any sinful speech﴾. And there will circulate among them young boys belonging to them, as if they were pearls well-guarded. And they will turn to one another, asking each other. They will say: "Indeed we were before among our people, fearful."

And His saying ﴿Therein there will be no idle talk nor any sinful speech﴾ means: no vain speech will pass between them, nor any speech for which its speaker incurs sin, as occurs among drinkers in this world. Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is that they will not become intoxicated, so that there would arise from them idle speech or speech for which they would sin.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there will circulate among them young boys (ghilman) of their own, as if they were pearls well-guarded﴾. That is: protected and concealed from the sun and the wind, and from everything that would take away their purity and radiance and change them.

The Exalted said: ﴿And they will approach one another, questioning each other.﴾ In the verse there is evidence that the people of Paradise gather together, recall the circumstances of the worldly life, and ask one another about them.

And as for His saying: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we were before this, among our families, fearful."﴾ Meaning: trembling and apprehensive. It is said that their fear and trepidation was on account of the Day of Resurrection. It is also said that their fear and trepidation was lest their deeds not be accepted from them, and this is in the sense of the Most High's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are fearful (mushfiqun) out of awe of their Lord﴾. 'Aisha said: "They did what deeds of obedience they did, yet feared that they would not be accepted from them." It is also said: the believer is trembling within his own home, because he needs to associate with his family and children, and he must, along with that, fear God the Most High, and not say or do anything that God does not approve of. And this is the most difficult thing for the believers: to be on guard before their Lord and to seek His pleasure in their affairs among people.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 27:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So God has been gracious to us﴾, meaning: God has bestowed His favour upon us.

And His saying: ﴿and has protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾, meaning: the punishment of Hell. It is said that al-Samum is one of the names of Hell. It is also said: "the punishment of the samum" means the punishment of the samum of Hell.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him before﴾, meaning: we used to declare Him one and worship Him. Here "du'a" (calling upon) carries the meaning of tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), and most of the exegetes hold this view. It is also said that it is the well-known meaning of du'a (supplication).

His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is He, the Good, the Merciful﴾. It is read with both the fath (opening) and the kasra (kasra) of the alif. Whoever reads it with the kasra, it is in the sense of a new beginning and resumption. Whoever reads it with the fath, its meaning is: we used to call upon Him before, because He is the Good, the Merciful, that is, because He is. Al-Barr (the Good) is the one who is benevolent and gentle toward His servants, and His gentleness toward His servants is His bestowing favours upon them despite the greatness of their sins and offences. Al-Rahim (the Merciful) is the one who is compassionate, in the sense we have mentioned. It is reported from some of them that al-Barr is the one who fulfils His promise to His friends.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the punishment of al-Samum, that he said: al-Samum is the seventh and uppermost layer of Hell. Al-Samum may occur with heat and may occur with cold.

The poet said:

(Today is a day whose samum is cold... whoever despairs today, I do not blame him.)

It is also said: al-Samum is the blaze of the fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 29:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So remind, for by the grace of your Lord you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman.﴾ His words ﴿so remind﴾ mean: admonish. It is also said: mention the punishment of the disbelievers and the bliss of the believers.

As for His words ﴿neither a soothsayer nor a madman﴾: the kahin (soothsayer) is the one who reports the unseen falsely. It is said: "takahhana kahanah" when he does that. And the majnun (madman) is the one whose intellect has departed and become confused.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet; we await for him the vicissitudes of fate"?﴾ It is said that "am" (or) here carries the meaning of interrogation, i.e., "Do you say, 'A poet'?" It is also said that the meaning is "bal" (rather). Al-Nahhas said: "aw" (or) in the language is used for moving from one topic to another.

His saying: ﴿A poet; we await for him the vicissitudes of fate﴾ means: the calamities of time.

Al-Khalil said: al-manun is death; Ibn al-Sikkit also mentioned this. It was also said that it is the changing of time (al-dahr). The poet said:
"Shall we grieve over al-manun and its vicissitudes?
Death is not one who blames the one who laments."

Al-manun is feminine and masculine. Whoever treats it as masculine does so according to the wording, and whoever treats it as feminine does so because it means al-maniyyah (death). It is also said that the "rayb" (vicissitudes) of al-manun is the time, the adversities of time. One says "rabani kadha," meaning: it befell me from it what I disliked.

In the exegesis it is reported that this statement was made by Abu Jahl, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and others. They said: "He is a poet; we await for him the calamities of time, and we will be rid of him by them, just as we were rid of so-and-so and so-and-so."

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say: "Wait, then"﴾, that is: wait (for what is coming).

﴿Indeed, I am with you among those who wait﴾, that is: those who wait. His waiting was either that he would gain victory over them or that they would submit.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 32:

And His Exalted saying: ﴿Or do their minds command them to this?﴾ That is: their intellects (ʿuqūl). They used to claim that they were people of intellect and forbearance (aḥlām). Al-ʿAql (intellect) is what calls to ḥilm (forbearance), so He named it by its name. It is also said that the meaning of this is to demean them and to declare them ignorant, that is: they have neither forbearance nor intellect, since they said such a statement, and since they ascribed to poetry and madness the one who called them to monotheism and brought them the proofs.

And His saying: ﴿Or are they a transgressing people?﴾ That is: rather, they are a transgressing people.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 33:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ That is: he has fabricated it and made it up.

And His saying: ﴿Rather, they do not believe﴾ That is: they do not affirm it as true.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it, if they are truthful﴾, meaning: a book like what Muhammad brought, if they are truthful that he fabricated it and invented it. This carries the sense of a challenge (tahaddi), as He mentioned in many places.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 35:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Or were they created from nothing?﴾ On this there are two opinions. The first is that its meaning is: Or were they created without having a creator and maker, that is, did they come into being by themselves?

And His words: ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ meaning: Did they create themselves? The intended sense according to this opinion is that, since they do not claim that they came into being without a creator and maker, nor do they claim that they are the ones who created themselves, and they acknowledge that their creator is Allah, then they should not worship anything alongside Him.

The second opinion is that its meaning is: Or were they created from nothing, that is, for no purpose? This is like the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose?﴾ and like His words: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾

If someone asks: Is it permissible for "min" (from) to carry the meaning of "li" (for)? The answer: some scholars have permitted this, and whoever did not permit it said that the meaning is: Or were they created from nothing that wisdom requires, meaning: wisdom required their creation. This was also mentioned by al-Nahhas, and the first opinion is more apparent in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 36:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Or were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ Its meaning: Or do they claim that the heavens and the earth were created for the idols they worship?

His words ﴿Rather, they do not have certainty﴾: that is, they do not have certainty regarding what they claim. It was also said: "Or were they created from nothing?" means: Are they the ones who created the heavens and the earth? Its meaning: they did not create the heavens and the earth.

In the (tafsir) it is related that they used to affirm that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth. So the meaning is: if they affirm that Allah is the Creator, why do they associate with Him another?!

Allah's statement: ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ That is, the gifts of your Lord. It is also said: His treasuries are of provision and rain, so do they possess them and give to whomever they wish?

His statement: ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ That is, the lords who hold dominion. Abu 'Ubayda said: the meaning is that they are not so. It is said: "tasaytara al-rajul 'ala fulan" (he dominated so-and-so), when he compelled him to do what he loves and desires.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 38:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they have a ladder?﴾ That is: a staircase and a means of ascent.

And his saying: ﴿by which they listen⁠—﴾ That is: upon it. It is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾, that is: upon the trunks of palm trees.

And his saying: ﴿then let their listener bring a clear authority﴾ That is: let whoever among them claims to have listened bring a clear proof. And in some of the tafsirs: just as Jibril brought the proof that he had heard the Revelation.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿Has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ Its meaning is: How can you claim that He has daughters when you yourselves do not accept that for yourselves? The meaning is: the matter is not as you claim.

Almost, but I should note one thing about the text itself: the second quotation is marked with curly braces rather than ﴿ ﴾, and it is the verse's wording, so I will render it with the ﴿ ﴾ markers as the instructions require.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 40:**

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ That is: a reward for conveying the message.

And His words ﴿so that they are burdened by a debt?﴾ That is: they are burdened by the debt that has befallen them. It is said: a crushing debt, or a heavy debt, has befallen so-and-so, and so he is burdened (*muthqal*).

Almighty God's words: ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ Its meaning: the knowledge of the unseen. It is also said: the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), so that they copy from it what they claim and assert. Its meaning is also: they do not have that; they have made the claims they made and said what they said as falsehood and lies. It is also said: "Or do they have the unseen?" means: a book from God, so that they say what they say from it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 42:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ That is: a plot against you (ﷺ). Their plot is what they devised concerning his affair, to expel him from Makkah, or to kill him, or to imprison him.

And His saying: ﴿Then those who disbelieve, they are the ones who will be ensnared.﴾ That is: they are the ones who will be killed, and they were killed at Badr. It is also said: its meaning is that Our plot and Our scheme will descend upon them.

Almighty God's saying: ﴿Or have they a god other than God?﴾ If it is said: they used to claim that they had gods other than God, so how is it correct to say, "Or have they a god other than God who gives life and causes death, who gives and withholds, who provides sustenance and deprives"?

And His saying: ﴿Glory be to God above what they associate with Him﴾ — He declared Himself exalted above their association (with Him) and above what they believed of worshipping other than Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 44:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky falling﴾. That is: a side of the sky, or a piece of the sky. He said this because some of the disbelievers said: ﴿So make a fragment of the sky fall upon us, if you are among the truthful﴾. The meaning is that if a side of the sky were to fall upon them, and they remained in it ascending, they would say: "Our eyes have only been intoxicated."

Almighty God's words: ﴿So leave them until they meet their Day, in which they will be struck senseless﴾. It is recited "yuṣ'aqūn" (they will be struck), meaning: they will die. It is also said: it is the Day of Resurrection, and "yuṣ'aqūn" is the descent of punishment upon them.

Almost-literal translation follows.

God's words, "On a day when their scheming will avail them nothing at all." That is, their stratagem.

And His words, "nor will they be helped." That is, nothing will prevent the punishment from them. It is also said: there will be no helper for them who can ward off (the punishment) from them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 47:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed for those who have done wrong is a punishment short of that﴾. The majority of scholars hold that it is the punishment of the grave. It is narrated from Mujahid that it is hunger in this world. It is also said: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾, meaning they do not know that the punishment is descending upon them. This is evidence that among them there were those who were obstinate, who recognised (the truth) and yet denied it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 48:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And be patient for the command of your Lord﴾, i.e., for what He has decreed upon you. This is consolation and solace for him concerning the harm that the disbelievers used to inflict upon him.

And His saying: ﴿For indeed, you are under Our eyes﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: in plain sight of Us. It is also said: We see you, protect you, and watch over you. The scholars of ma'ani (meanings of the Qur'an) said: He said this only to make the matter easy for him and to facilitate it, because when he knows that the harm inflicted on him by the disbelievers is by the decree of God and in His sight, it becomes somewhat easier for him, for He will not leave their recompense for that, nor His reward for him for the harm that befell him.

And His saying: ﴿And glorify your Lord with praise﴾, i.e., pray while praising your Lord.

It is related from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that its meaning is: when he stands for prayer he says: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You."

And it is related from some of them that when he stands for prayer he says: "Allahu akbar kabiran, wal-hamdu lillahi kathiran, wa subhan Allahi bukratan wa asilan," and this is what is meant by the verse; this was said by Zirr ibn Hubaysh. Abu al-Ahwas said its meaning is: that he says "Subhanaka wa bihamdika" whenever he stands up from any gathering. And it is related from some of them that he says, when he stands up from a gathering: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, la ilaha illa Anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk." This is an expiation for every gathering a person sits in.

And His saying: ﴿When you arise﴾ — we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 52, verse 49:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾ mean: pray to Him. It is also said that it refers to the Maghrib and the 'Isha' prayers. Mujahid said: it is the whole night.

And His words: ﴿and at the setting of the stars﴾. 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas said: it refers to the two rak'ahs before the dawn (Subh). It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and everything in it."

Accordingly, the meaning of "the retreat of prostrations" (idbar al-sujud) is the two rak'ahs of Maghrib, as Ibn 'Abbas said, and "the retreat of the stars" (idbar al-nujum) is the two rak'ahs of Subh. He called them "the retreat of the stars" because a person prays them when the stars' dominion of light departs, just as a man turns away from something and its authority over him ceases. It is also said that the meaning of His words ﴿and at the setting of the stars﴾ is the glorification (tasbih) after the Subh prayer.
